title: Prelaunch capacity & bottleneck mitigation plan
body:
Purpose
This sheet captures the pre-launch capacity assessment, KPI thresholds, and a prioritized mitigation playbook for the next product activation window. Goal: avoid user-facing degradations and keep per-token spend within forecasted bounds while reaching target activation throughput.

Quick summary and context
- Feature: dynamic routing + adaptive batching for hosted API  (pilot customer cohort).
- Launch window: M0+3 (soft launch to 10k DAUs, then scale to 100k DAUs over 6 weeks).
- Key risk: burst traffic patterns causing queue pileup and p99 latency > 800ms, leading to error ramp and cost overshoot.
- This doc combines a lightweight tracker (KPI snapshot), roadmap checkpoints, go/no-go criteria, and procedural mitigations (fast-fallback playbook).

KPI snapshot (current baseline -> target for soft launch)
- Target throughput: 120 reqs/s sustained (avg payload length 60 tokens)
- Baseline throughput (canary): 35 reqs/s
- P50 latency baseline: 85ms -> target <=120ms
- P95 latency baseline: 240ms -> target <=350ms
- P99 latency baseline: 520ms -> target <=800ms
- Error rate (5xx) baseline: 0.2% -> threshold alert at 1%
- Cache hit ratio baseline: 18% -> target >= 40%
- Average batch size baseline: 3.1 -> expected 4.8 under optimal batching
- Cost per 1k tokens baseline (hosted): $0.95 -> target <= $0.60 with batching/quantization

Acceptance / Go criteria for soft launch (must pass all):
1) Preflight load test: 2k concurrent virtual users with target distribution (see test plan) completes with p99 <= 900ms and error rate < 0.8%.
2) Autoscaler stability: no oscillation / 3x scale-down events in 15 minutes under steady ramp.
3) Monitoring: cache hit rate >= 30% on production canary for 48h.
4) Fallback validated: model-variant fallback returns compatible output and is tested end-to-end (sample prompts set).
5) Playbook drill: on-call and product ops execute a simulated incident runbook within 72h of go decision.

Roadmap checkpoints (milestones and owners)
- Week -4: Finalize surge simulation workload matrix (owner: Ravi Singh). Deliverable: synthetic load scripts + input corpus.
- Week -3: Complete optimization pass (intelligent batching + KV prefix caching tuning) (owner: Arjun Patel).
- Week -2: Run three progressive stress tests (smoke -> 25% load -> 100% load) and record token/cost burn (owner: Leah Gomez).
- Week -1: Canary deployment to customer cohort (owner: Priya Menon). Monitor 72h signals.
- Launch day: Activation cadence + throttles engaged (owner: Maya Thompson). Post-launch 8h war-room.

Contingency ladder (priority list when signals cross thresholds)
- Trigger levels and immediate response:
  - Alert A (soft, warning): p95 > 400ms for 10m or cache hit < 25% for 30m -> Run adaptive batch size increase (+1 token window), increase request coalescing TTL. Owner: infra on-call.
  - Alert B (urgent): p99 > 800ms or error rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> Activate model-variant fallback routing (route 20% traffic to smaller quantized model), enable aggressive KV cache warming, pause non-critical background tasks. Owner: SRE lead + product ops.
  - Alert C (critical): 5xx > 3% or outage -> Execute emergency throttle: drop low-priority routes (developer preview, background scoring), shift traffic to dedicated capacity region, notify sales/CS. Initiate rollback plan. Owner: exec on-call.

Fast-fallback recipe (step-by-step)
1) Detect & confirm (triage): check request-id sampling, confirm regressions across nodes and not a single-host anomaly.
2) Apply soft policy changes: increase batching window (from 10ms to 50ms), flip routing policy to prefer cached endpoints.
3) If soft policy fails > 5m: shift 20% traffic to quant-4bit variant (model alias: rwd-llm-small-q4).
4) If quant-variant shows significant semantic drift (manual spot-check fails): reduce to 10% and open immediate quality incident for product.
5) If error rates continue: engage throttle policy (token-based caps per api-key tier).

Metrics to log for post-incident RCA
- per-node qps, batch size distribution, cache hit/miss per prefix, median and tail latencies per model-variant, KV cache warm-up latency, cost per token by model variant, time-to-first-byte breakdown.

Surge simulation notes (results from preliminary runs)
- Sim run 2025-12-10 (synthetic spike): 3x baseline sustained for 12m. Observed: batch size collapsed to 1.2 under random arrival pattern -> p99 climbed to 1.4s. Primary contributor: poor coalescing when request jitter high.
- Experiment outcome: enabling lease-based coalescing + 12ms jitter buffer kept average batch size at 3.9 and reduced p99 to 680ms.
- Action: ship coalescing flag to canary, include jitter buffer param in prod config (default 12ms).

Open action items (owner and ETA)
- Infra: Implement lease-based coalescing flag and expose TTL knob in console. Owner: Arjun. ETA: 2025-11-18.
- Product: Curate 200 canonical prompts for fallback quality checks. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2025-11-05.
- SRE: Create escalation alert group and Slack runbook (auto-mention pager and product-ops). Owner: Leah. ETA: 2025-11-10.
- Finance: Update cost model for quantized variants and run sensitivity across 3 usage shapes. Owner: Ravi. ETA: 2025-11-12.

Notes to self (informal)
- Confirm the canary cohort's traffic profile matches expected burstiness (do not rely solely on average RPS).
- We need a small but explicit set of 'representative' prompts that exercise long-context retrieval and heavy KV cache paths.
- Pair with Solutions Eng for pre-baked fallback messaging for customers (what to communicate if we throttle).

Appendix: quick checklist for Go/No-Go meeting
- [ ] Surge sim pass with p99 <= 900ms and errors < 0.8%
- [ ] Autoscaler lookback shows no thrash in 2h steady-state test
- [ ] Cache warming strategy validated (>=30% hit)
- [ ] Fallback variant validated with 100 sample prompts
- [ ] Runbook tested with on-call (one dry-run)
- [ ] Finance sign-off on worst-case cost delta

Links and references
- Load test plan: JIRA POPS-4321
- Canary run dashboard (live): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/launch/canary-traffic
- Postmortem template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Incident+Postmortem+Template

Last notes: this is intentionally compact — keep it live and small. We'll expand the sheet into a more tabular tracker if the canary proves stable.

-- Maya
